text:
michael.green: Quick payroll/tax q. My spouse started a remote job based in Germany and is getting paid in EUR there. We're married filing jointly in the US. Concerned about withholding, foreign tax credit, and whether Redwood should adjust my W-4 or estimated payments. Any guidance? cc @lina.payroll

lina.payroll: Congrats to you both. Short: spouse foreign income doesn't change your Redwood W-4 directly. But combined household tax liability can change, so many couples adjust withholding or make estimated tax payments. We can run a projection if you share rough numbers (spouse gross EUR, any German tax withheld).

sophie.tax: A couple of flags: 1) US taxes worldwide apply, so you'll report spouse's foreign income on your joint return. 2) You can claim Foreign Tax Credit (FTC) for German income taxes paid, or opt for the Foreign Earned Income Exclusion (FEIE) if qualifying — but FEIE requires spouse to meet bona fide residence or physical presence tests. 3) FTC vs FEIE choice affects whether you should increase US withholding or use estimated payments.

michael.green: Spouse gross ~€62k/yr, German tax withheld ~€14k/yr. They will be tax resident in Germany. We plan to file jointly. What do you recommend?

sophie.tax: Quick math: €14k foreign tax on €62k likely gives a sizable FTC which can offset US tax on that income. If you file jointly, the FTC will typically prevent double taxation. However, sometimes FEIE + partial FTC hybrid is optimal. For accuracy we need estimates of other US-source income, deductions, and credits. If you expect low US tax on top of foreign income, you might not need to change withholding, but estimated payments can avoid underpayment penalties.

lina.payroll: If you want, Payroll can run a year-end projection and suggest a recommended additional withholding amount for your payroll or recommend quarterly estimated payments. To run it we'll need: 1) your annual salary, 2) spouse foreign gross and foreign tax withheld (you gave), 3) filing status (MFJ), 4) any large deductions.

michael.green: My salary $155k, no major itemized deductions planned. Please run the projection.

sophie.tax: Also decide whether spouse will claim FEIE. If they claim FEIE (Form 2555) for the €62k, that excludes up to the FEIE limit (indexed) from US tax, but then you can't claim FTC on excluded income. Often couples choose FTC for higher-rate foreign taxes. Given €14k paid, FTC likely better. We'll model both scenarios.

kevin.hr: Also note visa/immigration considerations if spouse is on a work permit tied to Germany. Not payroll but helpful for overall planning.

payroll-bot: Case logged: INT-TAX-6783. Assigned: lina.payroll and sophie.tax. ETA: projection within 3 business days. Please upload spouse paystub and year-to-date tax withholding to the HR portal for accuracy.

michael.green: Uploading stub now. Thanks team :)
